passages.text: O that you were to me like a brother who nursed at my mother’s breasts! If I found you outdoors, I would kiss you, and no one would despise me.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks to her beloved.
She wishes he were like a brother to her.
She wants him to be as close as a brother who nursed at her mother’s breasts.
She says, “If I found you outside, I would kiss you.”
She says, “No one would despise me for this.”
passages.original: מִ֤י יִתֶּנְךָ֙ כְּאָ֣ח לִ֔י יוֹנֵ֖ק שְׁדֵ֣י אִמִּ֑י אֶֽמְצָאֲךָ֤ בַחוּץ֙ אֶשָׁ֣קְךָ֔ גַּ֖ם לֹא־ יָב֥וּזוּ לִֽי׃

passages.text: I would lead you and bring you to the house of my mother who taught me. I would give you spiced wine to drink, the nectar of my pomegranates.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks to her beloved.
She says, "I would lead you."
She says, "I would bring you to my mother's house."
Her mother taught her there.
She says, "I would give you spiced wine to drink."
She says, "I would give you the nectar of my pomegranates."
passages.original: אֶנְהָֽגֲךָ֗ אֲבִֽיאֲךָ֛ אֶל־ בֵּ֥ית אִמִּ֖י תְּלַמְּדֵ֑נִי אַשְׁקְךָ֙ מִיַּ֣יִן הָרֶ֔קַח מֵעֲסִ֖יס רִמֹּנִֽי׃

passages.text: His left hand is under my head, and his right arm embraces me.
passages.sermon: The beloved is a man.\r\nHe places his left hand under my head.\r\nHe embraces me with his right arm.

passages.text: O daughters of Jerusalem, I adjure you: Do not arouse or awaken love until the time is right.
passages.sermon:
The speaker addresses the daughters of Jerusalem.
The speaker gives them a solemn warning.
The speaker says, “Do not awaken love.”
The speaker says, “Do not stir up love.”
The speaker says, “Wait until love desires to be awakened.”
The speaker teaches them to wait for the right time for love.
The speaker urges patience and restraint regarding love.
passages.original: הִשְׁבַּ֥עְתִּי אֶתְכֶ֖ם בְּנ֣וֹת יְרוּשָׁלִָ֑ם מַה־ תָּעִ֧ירוּ׀ וּֽמַה־ תְּעֹֽרְר֛וּ אֶת־ הָאַהֲבָ֖ה עַ֥ד שֶׁתֶּחְפָּֽץ׃ס

passages.text: Who is this coming up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? I roused you under the apple tree; there your mother conceived you; there she travailed and brought you forth.
passages.sermon:
A woman comes up from the wilderness.
She leans on her beloved.
I awakened you under the apple tree.
Your mother conceived you there.
Your mother labored and gave birth to you there.
passages.original: מִ֣י זֹ֗את עֹלָה֙ מִן־ הַמִּדְבָּ֔ר מִתְרַפֶּ֖קֶת עַל־ דּוֹדָ֑הּ תַּ֤חַת הַתַּפּ֙וּחַ֙ עֽוֹרַרְתִּ֔יךָ שָׁ֚מָּה חִבְּלַ֣תְךָ אִמֶּ֔ךָ שָׁ֖מָּה חִבְּלָ֥ה יְלָדַֽתְךָ׃

passages.text: Set me as a seal over your heart, as a seal upon your arm. For love is as strong as death, its jealousy as unrelenting as Sheol. Its sparks are fiery flames, the fiercest blaze of all.
passages.sermon:
The speaker is a woman who loves her beloved deeply.
She says, "Set me as a seal over your heart."
She also says, "Set me as a seal upon your arm."
Love is as strong as death.
Jealousy is as unyielding as the grave.
Love burns with fiery flames.
Love blazes with the fiercest fire.
passages.original: שִׂימֵ֨נִי כַֽחוֹתָ֜ם עַל־ לִבֶּ֗ךָ כַּֽחוֹתָם֙ עַל־ זְרוֹעֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־ עַזָּ֤ה כַמָּ֙וֶת֙ אַהֲבָ֔ה קָשָׁ֥ה כִשְׁא֖וֹל קִנְאָ֑ה רְשָׁפֶ֕יהָ רִשְׁפֵּ֕י אֵ֖שׁ שַׁלְהֶ֥בֶתְיָֽה׃

passages.text: Mighty waters cannot quench love; rivers cannot sweep it away. If a man were to give all the wealth of his house for love, his offer would be utterly scorned.
passages.sermon:
Love is powerful.
Mighty waters cannot put out love.
Rivers cannot wash love away.
No force can destroy true love.
If a man gives all his wealth for love, people will despise his offer.
No one can buy love with riches.
Love is beyond price.
passages.original: מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֗ים לֹ֤א יֽוּכְלוּ֙ לְכַבּ֣וֹת אֶת־ הָֽאַהֲבָ֔ה וּנְהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּהָ אִם־ יִתֵּ֨ן אִ֜ישׁ אֶת־ כָּל־ ה֤וֹן בֵּיתוֹ֙ בָּאַהֲבָ֔ה בּ֖וֹז יָב֥וּזוּ לֽוֹ׃ס

passages.text: We have a little sister, and her breasts are not yet grown. What shall we do for our sister on the day she is spoken for?
passages.sermon:
We have a little sister.
She is young.
Her breasts are not yet grown.
One day, someone will ask to marry her.
What should we do for our sister on that day?
passages.original: אָח֥וֹת לָ֙נוּ֙ קְטַנָּ֔ה וְשָׁדַ֖יִם אֵ֣ין לָ֑הּ מַֽה־ נַּעֲשֶׂה֙ לַאֲחֹתֵ֔נוּ בַּיּ֖וֹם שֶׁיְּדֻבַּר־ בָּֽהּ׃

passages.text: If she is a wall, we will build a tower of silver to protect her. If she is a door, we will enclose her with panels of cedar.
passages.sermon:
The speaker talks about a young sister.
The sister is not yet mature.
The speaker considers how to care for her.
If the sister is like a wall, she is strong and guarded.
We will build a tower of silver on her.
This will add to her strength and honor.
If the sister is like a door, she is open and accessible.
We will enclose her with panels of cedar.
This will protect her and keep her safe.
passages.original: אִם־ חוֹמָ֣ה הִ֔יא נִבְנֶ֥ה עָלֶ֖יהָ טִ֣ירַת כָּ֑סֶף וְאִם־ דֶּ֣לֶת הִ֔יא נָצ֥וּר עָלֶ֖יהָ ל֥וּחַ אָֽרֶז׃

passages.text: I am a wall, and my breasts are like towers. So I have become in his eyes like one who brings peace.
passages.sermon:
A woman speaks.
She says, "I am a wall."
She says, "My breasts are like towers."
He sees me as one who brings peace.
passages.original: אֲנִ֣י חוֹמָ֔ה וְשָׁדַ֖י כַּמִּגְדָּל֑וֹת אָ֛ז הָיִ֥יתִי בְעֵינָ֖יו כְּמוֹצְאֵ֥ת שָׁלֽוֹם׃פ

passages.text: Solomon had a vineyard in Baal-hamon. He leased it to the tenants. For its fruit, each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was a king of Israel.
Solomon owned a vineyard.
The vineyard was in Baal-hamon.
Solomon leased the vineyard to tenants.
Each tenant had to bring fruit from the vineyard.
Each tenant had to pay a thousand shekels of silver for the fruit.
passages.original: כֶּ֣רֶם הָיָ֤ה לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ בְּבַ֣עַל הָמ֔וֹן נָתַ֥ן אֶת־ הַכֶּ֖רֶם לַנֹּטְרִ֑ים אִ֛ישׁ יָבִ֥א בְּפִרְי֖וֹ אֶ֥לֶף כָּֽסֶף׃

passages.text: But my own vineyard is mine to give; the thousand shekels are for you, O Solomon, and two hundred are for those who tend its fruit.
passages.sermon:
I have my own vineyard.
My vineyard belongs to me.
I choose what to do with it.
Solomon, you receive a thousand shekels.
The people who care for the vineyard receive two hundred shekels.
They receive this for tending its fruit.
passages.original: כָּרְמִ֥י שֶׁלִּ֖י לְפָנָ֑י הָאֶ֤לֶף לְךָ֙ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה וּמָאתַ֖יִם לְנֹטְרִ֥ים אֶת־ פִּרְיֽוֹ׃

passages.text: You who dwell in the gardens, my companions are listening for your voice. Let me hear it!
passages.sermon: A woman lives in the gardens.\r\nHer friends listen for her voice.\r\nI ask her to let me hear her voice.
passages.original: הַיוֹשֶׁ֣בֶת בַּגַּנִּ֗ים חֲבֵרִ֛ים מַקְשִׁיבִ֥ים לְקוֹלֵ֖ךְ הַשְׁמִיעִֽינִי׃

passages.text: Come away, my beloved, and be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices.
passages.sermon:
My beloved, I speak to you now.
I ask you to come away.
Be swift and graceful.
Be like a gazelle.
Be like a young stag.
Go to the mountains of spices.
passages.original: בְּרַ֣ח׀ דּוֹדִ֗י וּֽדְמֵה־ לְךָ֤ לִצְבִי֙ א֚וֹ לְעֹ֣פֶר הָֽאַיָּלִ֔ים עַ֖ל הָרֵ֥י בְשָׂמִֽים׃
